fields: Without answer choices, what is the best architecture response to this scenario? A team tells Claude Code “never touch production,” but every developer environment has production admin credentials. What is strongest?
Remove/restrict production credentials and permissions; keep the instruction as supplemental guidance. Hard permission boundaries should not depend on model compliance.

Resolve this production scenario for team-level Claude tools and environments: Each developer has a different MCP/tool configuration and shared workflows behave inconsistently. What should the team do?
Standardize high-value repository/team configuration and version it. Shared configuration improves reproducibility and governance.

What should an architect recommend in this team-level Claude tools and environments situation? A third-party Skill contains scripts and external resources. What should happen before team-wide adoption?
Review provenance/content, test it, and constrain permissions appropriately. Skills can affect behavior and execution and should be governed.
Instruction — D7.1 application
Guidance intended to influence model behavior.
Runtime control — D7.1 application
An enforceable runtime, permission, sandbox, policy, or CI boundary.

Without answer choices, what is the best architecture response to this scenario? An agent writes a large refactor and tests pass, but nobody reviews whether the tests cover the risk. What is missing?
Independent human/system verification of both the change and test adequacy. Passing tests are evidence, not a substitute for judging whether verification is sufficient.
Resolve this production scenario for AI-assisted developer workflows: A developer asks an agent to “make it work” using production admin credentials. What is the strongest correction?
Use a scoped development/test environment and require approval for shared/destructive actions. Developer productivity should not expand unnecessary production capability.

What should an architect recommend in this AI-assisted developer workflows situation? AI-generated code is merged, but no team member understands it well enough to maintain it. What principle was violated?
Reviewability and human accountability for the change. Teams must be able to own and maintain generated changes.
Verification tool — D7.2 application
An independent mechanism such as tests, linters, type checks, security scans, or CI used to check generated changes.
Reviewability — D7.2 application
The ability for developers to understand and own an AI-generated change.

Without answer choices, what is the best architecture response to this scenario? Quality drops after a deployment. Which evidence should be checked first?
Model/prompt versions, retrieval/index changes, traces, and input-distribution changes around the deployment. Debugging starts from correlated evidence around the affected layer/change.
Resolve this production scenario for debugging and operational issue resolution: An agent suddenly receives “permission denied” from a tool. What areas are most relevant?
Credentials, scopes, authorization policy, tool contract, and dependency status. Tool failures should be diagnosed at the integration/permission boundary.
What should an architect recommend in this debugging and operational issue resolution situation? A cross-tenant data leak is observed. How should it be treated?
As a security incident focused on authorization/filtering boundaries, with containment and evidence preservation. Cross-tenant exposure is a security boundary failure.
Operational runbook — D7.3 application
Documented operational steps for diagnosis, mitigation, rollback/fallback, escalation, and evidence preservation.
verification — D7.3 application
